fields.rationale: States cluster around whether they require a formal bilateral reciprocity agreement, rely solely on equivalency of standards without a formal agreement, use an endorsement/credential-review model, combine exam waiver with equivalency checks, or apply near-automatic universal recognition; these five patterns cover the real variation without forcing unrelated values into a catch-all.

assignments.raw_value: Applicant must be licensed as an electrical administrator or equivalent in another state or territory, meet AK qualifications, and have passed an equivalent examination. If all three are met, the examination is waived.

Board may recognize a license issued by any other state with standards of practice or licensure equal to or higher than Alabama's. The board shall actively seek to reciprocate with qualifying states and maintain existing agreements.
Applicant must hold an equivalent license in another state; proof of that license must be submitted with required fees; and a reciprocity agreement must exist between Arkansas and that state.

Reciprocal licensure available if the other state accepts CA qualifications and the board ascertains that professional qualifications and conditions of good standing are at least the same or greater in that state as in California. Trade examination may be waived if applicant provides written certification of good standing for the previous five years.

License by endorsement: substantially equivalent credentials and qualifications. License by reciprocity: reciprocal agreement must exist between Colorado board and the other state's board where qualifications are substantially equivalent.
Applicant must hold a similar license from a state with substantially similar or higher requirements, and that state must grant reciprocal licensure to CT licensees without examination.

Applicant must present proof of current licensure in good standing in another state, DC, or US territory with substantially similar standards. If standards are not substantially similar, applicant must have practiced for a minimum of 5 years after licensure.

Applicant must meet FL certification requirements and have passed a substantially equivalent exam from another state/territory, OR hold a valid license from another state with substantially equivalent criteria, OR have held a valid license from another state for at least 10 years. Must also complete a 2-hour course on the Florida Building Code.
Reciprocity available where the other state has requirements substantially equal to Georgia's requirements and a similar privilege is offered to Georgia residents.
Licensure by endorsement or reciprocity available; expedited for nonresident military spouses under 436B-14.6 and 436B-14.7.

Reciprocal state must provide similar action; applicant must have been licensed in the other state for at least one year; must pay the required fee; must demonstrate qualifications equal to Iowa licensees of similar class.
Applicant must pay the required fee and furnish proof of qualifications at least equal to those required for written examination in Idaho. No written examination required for reciprocity applicants.

Applicant must be registered, licensed, or certified in another state with substantially equal requirements and be in good standing; the issuing state must extend similar reciprocity to Kentucky licensees.

Applicant must hold a comparable classification license in another state; the licensing state must certify in writing that the applicant passed the examination and is in good standing. The business law requirement is not waived. Applicants must comply with all other Louisiana licensing requirements.
Applicant must have been licensed as an electrician in another state under laws that, in the opinion of the examiners, maintain standards substantially the same as those of the commonwealth.

Applicant must hold an active license in good standing in another state equivalent to the MD license, meet the applicable experience requirements (7 years for master, 4 years for journeyperson), have been licensed in the other state by examination after meeting substantially equivalent requirements, and the other state must offer reciprocal examination waivers to MD licensees.

Applicant must be licensed in another state or territory with equivalent licensing standards and experience requirements; must have been licensed and actively engaged in electrician's work for a minimum of 8,000 hours; reciprocity is conditioned on the other jurisdiction granting similar privileges to Maine licensees. Board may waive the 576 hours of study requirement for journeyman or master license.

For sign specialty licensure, board and department may issue without examination if licensed in another state with equivalent or higher standards. For military members/veterans/dependents, license without examination available if requirements of other state are substantially equivalent. Temporary license available for out-of-state licensees in good standing.

Applicant must hold a valid comparable license in the qualifying state for at least one year continuously; qualifying state must administer a statewide licensing program with examination and qualifying experience comparable to Minnesota's; applicant must not have failed the same or greater class of license examination in Minnesota or had such license revoked or suspended; applicant must not have failed to renew for two or more years after expiration.

Other state's license standards must be substantially equivalent to or greater than Montana's standards, and there must be no reason to deny the license under Montana law. Applicant must affirm that verification from the other state has been requested.
Reciprocity available to the extent other states provide similar action; applicant must show qualifications equal to NC licensees and pay required fee; no written examination required.

Applicant must pay required fee and provide proof that their qualifications are equal to those of North Dakota licensees of the same grade or class. Reciprocity is available only to the extent the other state provides similar reciprocal action.
License granted if the other state's requirements are equivalent to or greater than NH's; board posts reciprocity information and lists of qualifying states on its website.

Reciprocity is discretionary; equal reciprocity must be provided by the other state or territory. Temporary licenses (up to 30 days) may be issued without examination to out-of-state individuals; beyond 30 days requires a full license application.
Reciprocal licensing agreement with states having equivalent licensing requirements; also expedited licensure available for military service members and veterans.

License by endorsement available for attainable housing projects in rural areas; applicant must hold valid unrestricted license in another state/territory with substantially similar qualifications, held for at least 4 consecutive years, with no disciplinary history. General license by endorsement also available under NRS 622.530 for any occupation regulated by the Board.

Written reciprocity agreement between states must exist; applicant must submit copy of agreement and pay licensure fee; electrical section must determine that other state's requirements are substantially equal to Ohio's and that other state extends similar reciprocity to Ohio licensees.

Applicant must have a valid license issued by another governmental entity with licensing requirements similar to those in the Electrical License Act, and must pay the license fee and comply with other provisions.

The administrator must determine that the other state's standards, qualifications and examinations are substantially similar to Oregon's; reciprocal agreement must be approved by the designated examining or advisory board.

Out-of-state license must be based on training equal to Rhode Island requirements. Military members and spouses licensed in another state for at least one year may receive a license if requirements are substantially equivalent.

Applicant must hold a license or certificate in good standing in another state with requirements equal to or greater than SC requirements; board must have authorized an exam waiver agreement. Applicant may also exempt the technical exam by verifying passage of an essentially equivalent exam in another state even without a reciprocal agreement. Applicant may still be required to pass the SC Commercial Contractors Business, Law and Project Management examination and must comply with all other licensing and certification requirements.
Reciprocal license available to the extent other states provide similar action; applicant must pay required fee and demonstrate qualifications equal to South Dakota holders of a similar license.
Applicant must hold a license in another state with which Texas has a reciprocity agreement recognizing licenses issued under this chapter, and submit a proper application and pay required fees.

License by endorsement available if: (1) similar scope of practice, (2) at least one year of experience under the other state's license, (3) license in good standing in issuing state; fee required; satisfactory evidence of identity, qualifications, and good standing

Universal license recognition: must hold current valid license in another state for at least 3 years, other state required exam and standards, no pending investigations, good standing, no disqualifying criminal record, no discipline (except financial-only), and payment of fees.

Reciprocal licensure available where the other state's standards are equivalent and grants similar privileges to VT licensees. Additionally, the Board shall issue a license to master and journeyman electricians licensed in good standing in another US jurisdiction for at least three years, regardless of reciprocity requirements.

Reciprocal agreements with other states whose requirements are equal to Washington standards; out-of-state applicants must provide evidence of equivalent qualifications and may receive a temporary permit while awaiting examination results.

fields.rationale: States cluster by whether the definition focuses narrowly on hands-on wiring work, adds planning/design/supervision, broadens to full electrical systems (generation, transmission, communication), uses a generic specialty-contractor framing, bundles multiple trades, explicitly calls out low-voltage/communications systems, or frames the scope around contracting business activities rather than the work itself.

assignments.raw_value: "electrical administrator" means a person who is responsible for (A) installing or repairing electrical wiring, conduits, devices, fixtures, equipment, or other electrical materials for transmitting, using, or consuming electrical energy; or (B) certifying that an installation or repair described in (A) of this paragraph complies with applicable electrical codes
Any job or project in the State of Alabama wherein the electrical contractor proposes to bid, install, maintain, alter, or repair any electric wiring devices or equipment.

"Electrical work" means: (A) Installations of electric conductors and equipment within or on public and private buildings or other structures, including recreational vehicles and floating buildings, and other premises such as yards, carnivals, parking and other lots, and industrial substations; (B) Installations of conductors that connect to the supply of electricity; and (C) Installations of other outside conductors on the premises;

Specialty commercial contracting, which is engaging in the contracting business in the performance of construction work requiring special skill and involving the use of specialized construction trades or crafts other than residential contracting.

A specialty contractor is a contractor whose operations involve the performance of construction work requiring special skill and whose principal contracting business involves the use of specialized building trades or crafts.
Electrical work means wiring for, installing, and repairing electrical apparatus and equipment for electric light, heat, and power.

"Electrical work" means the installation, erection, maintenance, inspection, testing, alteration or repair of any wire, cable, conduit, busway, raceway, support, insulator, conductor, appliance, apparatus, fixture or equipment that generates, transforms, transmits or uses electrical energy for light, heat, power or other purposes, but does not include low voltage wiring, not exceeding twenty-four volts, used within a lawn sprinkler system

"Master electrician" shall mean a person, licensed by the Board, to plan, estimate, layout, perform or supervise the installation, erection or repair of any electrical conductor, molding, duct, raceway, conduit, machinery, apparatus, device or fixture for the purpose of lighting, heating or power in any structure.

"Electrical contractor" or "unlimited electrical contractor" means a person who conducts business in the electrical trade field and who has the experience, knowledge, and skill to install, repair, alter, add to, or design, in compliance with law, electrical wiring, fixtures, appliances, apparatus, raceways, conduit, or any part thereof, which generates, transmits, transforms, or utilizes electrical energy in any form, including the electrical installations and systems within plants and substations, all in compliance with applicable plans, specifications, codes, laws, and regulations.

Electrical contracting means the installation, maintenance, alteration, or repair of any electrical equipment, apparatus, control system, or electrical wiring device which is attached to or incorporated into any building or structure in this state but shall not include low-voltage contracting.

"Electrician" means any person who performs electrical work and includes but is not limited to any person who acts as a journey worker electrician, journey worker specialty electrician, supervising electrician, supervising specialty electrician, maintenance electrician, journey worker industrial electrician, or supervising industrial electrician.

No person shall, for another, wire for or install electrical wiring, apparatus, or equipment, or supervise an apprentice electrician or unclassified person, unless the person is licensed by the board as an electrical contractor, a class A master electrician, or a class B master electrician, or is licensed as a class A journeyman electrician or a class B journeyman electrician and is employed by an electrical contractor or is working under the supervision of a class A master electrician or a class B master electrician.

Any person who personally performs or supervises the actual physical work of installing electrical wiring or equipment to convey electric current, or apparatus to be operated by such current, or engages in planning, lay out, or design of such wiring, equipment, or apparatus, or the supervision thereof, shall for the purpose of this chapter be known as a journeyman electrician.

"Electrician" means any person licensed by the department who is employed by an electrical contractor and is engaged in the construction, alteration, or repair of any electrical system used for the purpose of furnishing heat, light, or power

"Electrical contractor" means any person who undertakes to, attempts to, or submits a price or bid or offers to construct, supervise, superintend, oversee, direct, perform, or in any manner assume charge of the construction, alteration, repair, improvement, movement, demolition, putting up, tearing down, or furnishing labor together with material and equipment, or installing the same for the wiring, fixtures, or appliances for the supply of electricity to any residential, commercial, or other project, for which the project value is ten thousand dollars or more.

a person qualified to do the work of installing, repairing, or maintaining wires, conduits, apparatus, devices, fixtures, or other appliances used for heat, light, power, fire warning or security system purposes

"Provide electrical services" means to provide any service in the electrical trade, including installing, repairing, maintaining, erecting, or altering any electrical equipment, wiring, fixture, appliance, apparatus, raceway, conduit, or system that generates, transmits, transforms, or uses electrical energy in any form for light, heat, power, or communication.

"Electrical installations" means the installation, repair, alteration and maintenance of electrical conductors, fittings, devices and fixtures for heating, lighting, power purposes or heat activated fire alarms, intrusion alarms, energy management, telephone, cable and closed-circuit television, sound systems, data transmission, conduit and raceway systems and electrically supervised manual fire alarms and sprinkler systems. "Electrical installations" includes complete installations related to photovoltaic, fuel cell and wind power generation systems.

"Electrical wiring" means all wiring, generating equipment, fixtures, appliances, devices, and appurtenances in connection with the generation, distribution, and utilization of electrical energy, in or on a building, residence, structure, or properties, regardless of whether or not the electrical wiring is energized at the time of installation.

Electrical work means the installing, altering, repairing, planning, or laying out of electrical wiring, apparatus, or equipment for electrical light, heat, power, technology circuits or systems, or other purposes.

"Electrical construction" means work performed by an individual, firm, or corporation in which an electrical connection is made to a supply of electricity or in which electricity is supplied to any electric equipment installation for which a permit is required by the authority having jurisdiction.

Electrical contracting shall be defined as engaging or offering to engage in the business of installing, maintaining, altering or repairing any electric work, wiring, devices, appliances or equipment.

plan, lay out, supervise, install, make additions, make alterations, or make repairs, in the installation of wiring, apparatus, or equipment for electric light, heat, or power or for a power limited system

Electrical installations means the installation, repair, alteration and maintenance of electrical conductors, fittings, devices and fixtures for heating, lighting or power purposes, regardless of the voltage.

"Electrical contractor" means a person who engages in the business of contracting to install, erect, repair or alter electrical equipment for the generation, transmission or utilization of electrical energy

"electrical wiring" means all wiring, conductors, fixtures, devices, conduits, appliances or other equipment, including generating equipment such as solar electricity generating equipment of not over ten kilowatt capacity, used in connection with the general distribution or use of electrical energy

A specialty contractor is a contractor whose operations as such are the performance of construction work requiring special skill and whose principal contracting business involves the use of specialized building trades or crafts.

"Licensed trade" means a trade performed by a heating, ventilating, and air conditioning contractor, a refrigeration contractor, an electrical contractor, a plumbing contractor, or a hydronics contractor.

Journeyman electrician means any person other than an electrical contractor who engages in the actual installation, alteration, repair or renovation of electrical facilities or electrical construction work unless specifically exempted by the provisions of the Electrical License Act

"Electrical installations" means the construction or installation of electrical wiring and the permanent attachment or installation of electrical products in or on any structure that is not itself an electrical product. "Electrical installation" also means the maintenance or repair of installed electrical wiring and permanently attached electrical products.
Journeyperson electrician means a person doing any work of installing wires, conduits, apparatus, fixtures, and other appliances.

"Electrical" which includes the installation, alteration, or repair of wiring-related electrical material and equipment used in the generating, transmitting, or utilization of electrical energy less than six hundred volts, including all overhead electrical wiring on public rights-of-way for signs and street decorations and all underground electrical distribution systems of less than six hundred volts serving private properties.

"Electrical contractor," a person having the necessary qualifications, training, experience, and technical knowledge to plan, lay out, and supervise the installation and repair of electrical wiring, apparatus, and equipment for electric light, heat and power in accordance with the standard rules governing such work; and who undertakes or offers to undertake with another to plan for, lay out, supervise and install or to make additions, alterations and repairs in the installation of such work

"Electrical work" means any labor or material used in installing, maintaining, or extending an electrical wiring system and the appurtenances, apparatus, or equipment used in connection with the use of electrical energy in, on, outside, or attached to a building, residence, structure, property, or premises. The term includes service entrance conductors as defined by the National Electrical Code.

"Electrical trade" means the performance of any electrical work involved in the installation, construction, alteration, change, repair, removal, or maintenance of facilities, buildings, or appendages or appurtenances.

"Tradesman" means any individual who engages in, or offers to engage in, work for the general public for compensation in the trades of electrical, plumbing and heating, ventilation and air conditioning.

"Electrical installation" means wires, fixtures, or apparatus installed in a complex structure or at the construction site of such structure for the transmission and use of commercially supplied or privately generated electrical energy.

"Electrical construction trade" includes, but is not limited to, installing or maintaining electrical wires and equipment that are used for light, heat, or power and installing and maintaining remote control, signaling, power limited, or communication circuits or systems.
